stem: Which example is an environmental barrier rather than a limitation of the person?

options.text: A single step at a building's main entrance.
options.rationale: The step is a feature of the built environment that excludes some people, and it can be removed or redesigned.
Reduced hearing is a sensory characteristic of the person, not a feature of the environment.

options.text: Chronic fatigue that limits physical activity.
options.rationale: Chronic fatigue is a health condition of the person; the barrier arises when the environment does not accommodate it.

options.text: Difficulty decoding long or unfamiliar words.
options.rationale: This is a cognitive or learning characteristic of the person, not an environmental obstacle.

explanation: Under the social model, disability arises from the interaction between a person and barriers in the environment. A step at an entrance is a design barrier that can be removed; reduced hearing, fatigue, and difficulty decoding words are characteristics of the person. The same characteristic may or may not become disabling depending on how the environment is designed.

references.title: W3C WAI — Diverse Abilities and Barriers

author: Oxypteros
